reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Code reading is correct but spec interpretation is wrong. The spec states 'If no schedule entry matches, defaults to ELECTRA parameters' (INV-004 in SG-001). The code returns Electra limit (9) when epoch >= ElectraForkEpoch (L719-720) and Deneb limit (6) otherwise (L723) when no BlobSchedule match exists. This epoch-conditional fallback is intentional and spec-compliant for pre-Fulu networks. The spec INV-004 applies to Fulu-era behavior, not historical epoch handling.
reviewed_items.spec_reference: SG-001 INV-004: get_blob_parameters defaults to ELECTRA parameters when no BLOB_SCHEDULE matches; code implements epoch-aware fallback for backward compatibility.

reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Verified: validateDataColumnsByRange returns nil when endSlot < minStartSlot (L198-200), causing handler to return success with zero sidecars (L72-74). Spec requires ResourceUnavailable (code 0x03) per SG-008 q_error_unavailable transition. The spec diagram explicitly shows 'range outside serve_range => respond ResourceUnavailable(3)' but code sends success response.
reviewed_items.spec_reference: SG-008 q_error_unavailable: requests outside data_column_serve_range must receive ResourceUnavailable(3) response, not success with empty data.

reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Code reading verified: ComputeCells calls ckzg4844.ComputeCells (L58), creates output slice with len(ckzgCells) (L63), and iterates i := range ckzgCells (L64). The library contract guarantees exactly CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB cells for valid blobs per spec SG-018 INV-002. While no explicit bounds check exists, the library is cryptographically verified and panic would indicate library bug, not caller vulnerability. Defensive validation would be good practice but not a vulnerability.
reviewed_items.spec_reference: SG-018 INV-002: compute_cells output contains exactly CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB cells. Code trusts cryptographic library contract.

reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Phase 03 misread the architecture. ComputeForkDigest (L304-310) is the legacy helper per original spec, but the production ForkDigest lookup uses ForkDigestUsingConfig (fork.go:18-20) which retrieves precomputed digests from networkSchedule. The schedule builder (config.go:575-589) correctly XORs blob parameters for Fulu epochs (L586-589). Code paths like bootnode DO use the schedule-based ForkDigest, not ComputeForkDigest directly. Spec SG-003 requirement is met by network schedule, not the legacy helper.
reviewed_items.spec_reference: SG-003 INV-003: XOR with blob parameter hash ensures different configs produce different digests. Implemented in entryWithForkDigest (config.go:586-589), used by networkSchedule.

reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Verified: SidecarDescendsFromFinalized (L337-354) only checks fc.HasNode(parentRoot) (L348), which verifies parent exists in fork choice but does NOT verify finalized ancestry. Spec SG-006 q_check_finalized_ancestor requires 'finalized checkpoint not ancestor => REJECT'. The code skips the ancestor check entirely, allowing sidecars on non-finalized forks to pass gossip validation. This violates the spec's explicit requirement.
reviewed_items.spec_reference: SG-006 q_check_finalized_ancestor: gossip validation must verify 'finalized checkpoint is ancestor' of block root, rejecting if not. Code only checks parent existence.
